answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained useful work tied to a single identity. Each agent must complete verifiable tasks over time, building a reputation spiral where trust grows only gradually and cannot be bought instantly. A newcomer starts at dawn of its history with no privileges, so creating thousands of fakes yields empty histories, not influence. Like a raven known by its distinct call, each work trail is unique and costly to forge: faking it requires doing the work and paying compute and time per identity, making large-scale sybil attacks unprofitable.
